title: Live cell microscopy of mitochondria-lysosome contact site formation and tethering dynamics
protocol: Warm 9 mL of HeLa media in a 50 mL conical tube in a 37°C bath.
Thaw frozen vial of HeLa cells (1 mL) stored in liquid nitrogen tank by holding it in the 37°C bath for about 1 minute.
Immediately add thawed HeLa cells to 9 mL of warm HeLa media.
Spin down cells at 200 × g for 3 minutes to remove DMSO from the media.
Resuspend cell pellet in 5 mL of HeLa media and mix until homogeneous.
Resuspend cells again into a final total volume of 20 mL of HeLa media.
Plate HeLa cells into two 10 cm plates with 10 mL of media per plate.
Grow the cells in an incubator at 37°C for 2–3 days.
Warm HeLa media for at least an hour before passaging.
Examine cells under a cell culture microscope to ensure normal morphology, optimal confluency (80%–100%), and absence of contamination.
Aspirate off HeLa media from a confluent plate with a glass Pasteur pipet attached to the vacuum.
Wash cells with 5 mL of sterile PBS at 20°C and aspirate.
Add 2 mL of TrypLE Express (stored at 4°C) to detach cells from the plate.
Place cells in TrypLE Express in a CO2 incubator for 3 min to ensure complete detachment.
Add 5 mL of HeLa media to the plate containing TrypLE Express and resuspend media several times while rotating the cell dish.
Collect resuspended cells (∼7 mL total) into a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge cells at 200 × g at 20°C for 3 min.
Aspirate off media and TrypLE Express.
Add 5 mL of HeLa media to the conical tube containing the cell pellet.
Resuspend the mixture gently until homogeneous.
Dilute the cell suspension to a final volume of 40 mL with HeLa media.
Add 10 mL of the diluted cell suspension to each 10 cm dish for maintaining cell culture.
Add 1.5 mL of the diluted cell suspension to each 35 mm MatTek dish for live cell microscopy.
Incubate cells at 37°C until they reach approximately 70% confluency.
Avoid introducing bubbles into the media and dishes during handling.
Minimize movement of cell plates after initial passaging to prevent clumping.
Mix 100 μL Optimem and 0.5 μg DNA of each plasmid (Lamp1-mGFP and mApple-TOMM20) in a sterile Eppendorf tube.
Resuspend the mixture 5–6 times to ensure proper mixing.
In a separate sterile Eppendorf tube, mix 100 μL Optimem and 3 μL Lipofectamine 2000 (use 1.5 μL/plasmid).
Resuspend this mixture 5–6 times to ensure proper mixing.
Mix each tube individually.
Wait 5 minutes.
Combine solutions from both Eppendorf tubes.
Wait 20 minutes.
Resuspend the combined solution 5–6 times to ensure proper mixing.
Add the combined solution to cells plated in a 35 mm dish for live cell microscopy.
Transfect cells for 24–32 hours prior to imaging.
Sterilize the work area by spraying the microscope buttons and desk area with 70% EtOH.
Examine cells under a cell culture microscope to check for cell health and general morphology before imaging.
Set the microscope CO2 levels to 5% CO2 and the heater to 37°C for at least 30 min before imaging.
Turn on the Nikon A1R laser scanning confocal microscope.
Add Immersol immersion oil to the objective.
Place the live cell imaging plate into the heated microscope chamber.
Turn on the 488 nm laser.
Adjust the objective depth until the fluorescent plane is visible through the eyepiece.
Turn off the laser immediately after finding cells of interest.
Search for 10–15 viable cells to be used for live cell confocal movies.
Acquire images from a single z-plane for each selected cell.
Avoid imaging cells that are not adherent to the plate.
Exclude cells with high levels of autofluorescence.
Do not image cells with excessively high levels of fluorescent plasmid expression.
Take a confocal image of each previously selected cell.
Transfect HeLa cells with LAMP1-mGFP (lysosomal membrane) and mApple-TOMM20 (outer mitochondrial membrane).
Image the transfected HeLa cells using live cell confocal microscopy.
Acquire laser scanning confocal time-lapse movies visualizing lysosomes (Lamp1-mGFP) and mitochondria (mApple-TOMM20) with Green 488 nm and Red 561 nm lasers respectively.
Obtain movies at a minimum rate of 1 frame/2 s for 3 min to visualize mitochondria-lysosome contact site formation and dynamics.
Set the excitation wavelength to 561 nm.
Set the emission wavelength to 595 nm.
Adjust laser power to 3.0.
Set PMT HV (gain) to 15.
Set PMT offset to 0.
Standardize laser intensity, gain, and offset settings across cells and between plates.
Define mitochondria-lysosome contact sites as stable tethering for at least 10 seconds.
Limit live cell imaging duration to 1 hour per plate to avoid phototoxicity and photobleaching.
Save all confocal images and time-lapse movies acquired.
Remove the live cell imaging plate from the microscope chamber carefully.
Turn off CO2 supply, microscope heater, and Nikon A1R laser scanning confocal microscope.
